objective: Implement v0.3.4 distribution recovery so DSH Crew has a stable package-manager-installed launcher and working install/status/update/uninstall lifecycle that does not depend on broken npx transient-cache PATH behavior.
context: Issue #51 is authoritative product context. @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.3 is already public and latest=0.3.3; NEVER republish, deprecate, unpublish, or mutate 0.3.3. Its tarball was verified against immutable commit 369b141f7878e057d08c673fe90b62185e67fdeb. Public npx/npm exec fails before Crew code starts because the spawned command PATH does not resolve dsh-crew; direct execution of the published bin succeeds, and an isolated npm 12 check reproduces the npx failure. npm/cli issue #9870 documents this regression class. No v0.3.3 tag or GitHub Release exists and none should be created in this task. Recover the user experience around a stable globally/package-manager-installed dsh-crew launcher while preserving the durable Crew-owned payload under ~/.config/dsh-crew and the existing Harness-owned provider/model architecture.
forbidden_changes: publishing, republishing, deprecating, unpublishing, changing access/owners, or mutating dist-tags for any npm package/version
creating, moving, rewriting, or deleting any git tag or GitHub Release, including v0.3.3 and v0.3.4
reading, printing, hashing, copying, or mutating npm tokens, OTPs, auth headers, .npmrc contents, DSH credential contents, OpenCode auth stores, or other secrets
reading or mutating normal ~/.dsh, the official DSH web profile, or official DSH credentials
weakening or rewriting npm/pnpm security settings, lifecycle-script policy, minimum release age, global package-manager policy, or approving scripts globally
changing or relying on the unrelated unscoped dsh-crew npm package
validation: Validate the Task Contract before work and the Result Contract with --stamp before completion.
Run focused distribution/lifecycle/installer tests covering the package-manager-installed launcher, install, status, update, repair, uninstall, purge, and source-checkout compatibility.
Run node --test test/*.test.mjs and require zero failures.
Run pnpm run build:client and restore any generated drift so the completion checkout is clean except allowed intended changes.
Run pnpm run verify:npm-install and pnpm run verify:npm-install:official.

Pack the 0.3.4 candidate locally and run a real Windows disposable-prefix lifecycle that does not depend on npx command execution: npm install -g --prefix <disposable-prefix> <candidate-tarball>; invoke the generated dsh-crew command from that prefix; run install -> status -> update -> status -> uninstall -> status in a disposable HOME/USERPROFILE/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/TEMP.
Prove the durable Crew-owned installed payload still works after deleting the candidate tarball/pack directory and any task-created npx cache inputs.
Exercise a repair update after corrupting a managed payload/removing registration while proving config.json and .env (or equivalent sentinel config/credential-reference files) remain byte-identical.

Exercise update candidate resolution against a controlled local/registry-compatible candidate path or safe override so the test proves update can obtain a newer permitted package without requiring a source checkout and without changing global package-manager security configuration.
Run source-checkout node scripts/setup.mjs install/status/uninstall in a separate disposable home.

Run npm pack --dry-run --json and audit the package for required launcher/runtime/client/setup assets and absence of ACTIVE_TASK, agent results, tests, node_modules, tarballs, temp files, credentials/secrets, and .env.
Run npm publish --dry-run --access public only; perform no real publication.
Read-only verify public state: @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.3 remains present and latest=0.3.3, @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.4 remains absent, and no v0.3.4 tag/Release exists.
acceptance_criteria: Package/runtime/changelog identity is 0.3.4 and the packaged launcher exposes a callable dsh-crew command after a normal package-manager/global-prefix installation on Windows; Unix launcher/path behavior is covered by portable tests where a live host is unavailable.

The primary documented lifecycle is dsh-crew install, dsh-crew status, dsh-crew update, and dsh-crew uninstall after the stable launcher is installed; broken transient npx execution is not presented as the primary supported path while npm/cli #9870 remains unresolved.
First install remains as close to one command as practical and does not require cloning the repository or relying on npx transient-cache PATH execution.

The launcher/global package is not the authoritative runtime location: install/update stages and validates a durable Crew-owned payload under ~/.config/dsh-crew and registers Harness/integrations against that durable path.

dsh-crew status is read-only and reports launcher/candidate version, installed payload version/state, dedicated Harness registration, Codex integration, and Claude integration without reading secret contents.

dsh-crew update is a real update operation: it can resolve/stage/validate the newest permitted Crew package from a configured npm registry or equivalent safe candidate source, preserve user config/credential references, retain the prior usable payload until activation succeeds, repair stale registration, and remain idempotent when already current. It must not require a source checkout. If safe self-replacement of the globally installed launcher is intentionally not attempted, the limitation is explicit while the managed Crew payload still updates correctly.
dsh-crew uninstall removes the Crew-managed payload plus integrations/registration while preserving normal config/backups by default; --purge remains explicit.
Real disposable Windows lifecycle, repair behavior, full deterministic suite, client build, both npm install verifiers, pack audit, and publish dry-run all PASS with final_machine_state: INSTALLED.
No npm publication/dist-tag mutation, tag/Release mutation, credential access, official DSH mutation, or package-manager security-policy weakening occurs.
